repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until(not (all(#HumiditySensor).humiditySensor_humidity <= 30))
triggered = false
}
wait until(all(#HumiditySensor).humiditySensor_humidity <= 30)
all(#Switch).switch_on()
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR specifies a rising-edge wait (`wait(cond, edge rising)`), which requires blocking until the condition transitions from false to true. The candidate uses a periodic `if` statement that only evaluates at the start of each 1-second cycle. Evidence F2 shows the condition became true at 100ms, but the JoI missed the action because it wasn't waiting for the edge. The fix implements the standard rising-edge state machine: block until the condition is false, then block until it is true, then execute the body.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with a blocking two-wait rearm pattern. This ensures the automation waits for the specific rising edge (false-to-true transition) rather than just checking the value at arbitrary intervals.
